name: Refund / Tech-Support Swarm With Declarative Handoffs (Strategy.SWARM)
query: Support swarm in Python: a `refund_specialist` and a `tech_support` agent that can pass the customer to each other as the conversation develops. If the customer mentions a refund, go to refunds; if the `lookup_order` tool comes back saying the item was damaged, go to tech support. Refunds must be approved by a human, and nothing may loop forever. What does the SDK give me for this?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 (the `swarm` row: children pass control through compiler-injected `transfer_to_<peer>` tools; declarative `handoffs=[OnTextMention(...), OnToolResult(...)]`; gotchas — never name a tool `transfer_*` or an agent `done`; `OnCondition` handoffs are workers `serve()` registers; every open-ended strategy needs `max_turns` or `termination`), references/agents.md §4/§5 (handoff conditions, termination, `approval_required`), references/optimization.md F1, F2 (refund is a side-effect tool), F3 and F10 (`swarm` without `termination` is flagged).

Step 2: Two children with unique names, `provider/model`, instructions and their own `max_turns`; tools: `lookup_order` (`@tool`), `issue_refund` (`@tool(approval_required=True)` — F2), `open_ticket` (`@tool`). Tool names must not start with `transfer_`.

Step 3: `support = Agent(name="support_swarm", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", agents=[refund_specialist, tech_support], strategy=Strategy.SWARM, max_turns=6, handoffs=[OnTextMention(text="refund", target="refund_specialist"), OnToolResult(tool_name="lookup_order", result_contains="damaged", target="tech_support")])` with `from conductor.ai.agents import Agent, AgentRuntime, Strategy, OnTextMention, OnToolResult, OnCondition, tool`.

Step 4: Explain the mechanism: the compiler injects a `transfer_to_<peer>` tool into each child so the model itself can hand off; the declarative `handoffs` fire on text mentions / tool results; `OnCondition(callable, target=...)` exists for custom predicates and is a worker that `serve()` registers (worker gate). Do not name any agent `done`.
Step 5: Bounds (F1/F10): `max_turns=6` on the swarm plus, optionally, `termination=TextMentionTermination("RESOLVED") | MaxMessageTermination(12)`; each child has its own `max_turns`.

Step 6: Lifecycle: `runtime.run(support, ...)` under `if __name__ == "__main__":`; `runtime.deploy(support)`; long-lived `runtime.serve(support)` for the `@tool` workers and any `OnCondition` handoff. Never `conductor deploy`.

Step 7: Approval: when `issue_refund` is reached the run pauses with `waiting: true` + `pendingTool.toolCalls[].name == "issue_refund"`; approve with `conductor agent respond <id> --approve` / `POST /api/agent/{id}/respond {"approved": true}` — never via an AGENT resume (Rule 12 / F8).

Step 8: Any workflow call uses `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "support_swarm"`, `maxDurationSeconds`; never `agentType: "swarm"`. Verify offline with `mock_run(..., events=[MockEvent.handoff(...)])` + `expect(result).handoff_to("tech_support")`, live with the `handoff` event on `conductor agent stream`.
success_criteria: `handoffs=[...]` includes an `OnTextMention(text=..., target=...)` and an `OnToolResult(tool_name="lookup_order", result_contains="damaged", target=...)`
States that the compiler injects `transfer_to_<peer>` tools and therefore warns not to name custom tools `transfer_*` or an agent `done`
Sets `max_turns` on the swarm (and/or a `termination` condition) and states that an unbounded swarm is a problem (F1 / F10)
If `OnCondition` (callable predicate) handoffs are used, states they are workers that `serve()` registers — N/A and passing when only `OnTextMention` / `OnToolResult` are used

The refund side-effect tool is gated with `approval_required=True` (or a guardrail) per F2, and approval goes through `conductor agent respond --approve` / `POST /api/agent/{id}/respond {"approved": true}` — not an AGENT resume
Deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` and names a long-lived `runtime.serve(...)` for the `@tool` workers — never `conductor deploy`
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never `agentType: "swarm"` or a framework name
Each child has a unique `name` and its own `max_turns`, and a verification path is mentioned (`mock_run` + `handoff_to`, or the `handoff` stream event)
